[Section] Experiments ::: Error Analysis ::: False Negatives
[source_id=74] had two types:
[source_id=75] [leftmargin=*]
[source_id=76] Mixture of offensiveness and admiration: ex. calling a girl a puppy يا كلبوبة> (“yA klbwbp” – “O puppy”) in a flirtatious manner.
[source_id=77] Implicit offensiveness: ex. calling for cure while implying sanity in: وتشفي حكام قطر من المرض> (“wt$fy HkAm qTr mn AlmrD” – “and cure Qatar rulers from illness”).
[source_id=78] Many errors stem from heavy use of dialectal Arabic as well as ambiguity. Since BERT was trained on Wikipedia (MSA) and Google books, the model failed to classify tweets with dialectal cues. Conversely, Mazajak/SVM is more biased towards dialects, often failing to classify MSA tweets.
child_qasper_evidence_texts: Mixture of offensiveness and admiration: ex. calling a girl a puppy يا كلبوبة> (“yA klbwbp” – “O puppy”) in a flirtatious manner.
Implicit offensiveness: ex. calling for cure while implying sanity in: وتشفي حكام قطر من المرض> (“wt$fy HkAm qTr mn AlmrD” – “and cure Qatar rulers from illness”).

Many errors stem from heavy use of dialectal Arabic as well as ambiguity. Since BERT was trained on Wikipedia (MSA) and Google books, the model failed to classify tweets with dialectal cues. Conversely, Mazajak/SVM is more biased towards dialects, often failing to classify MSA tweets.
